source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 23. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Sidq: always telling the truth, no matter what

learn.en: Sidq means truthfulness. A sadiq is someone who tells the truth so often that it becomes his habit.
learn.title: Sidq

learn.en: Truthfulness means being the same inside and outside: what you believe in private is what you show in public.
learn.title: The same inside and out

learn.en: The Prophet ﷺ was the most truthful of all people. Allah is with those who are truthful.
learn.title: The most truthful

learn.en: Lying is like a drop of black ink: it spreads until it covers everything. The only cure is to stop lying and speak the truth.
learn.title: A drop of black ink

learn.en: Don't talk too much — it can lead to nonsense and lies. Words must be backed up by actions.
learn.title: Words and actions

learn.en: “O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true.” (Qur'an 9:119)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

quiz.en: You didn't finish your homework. You…
opts: apologise and tell the teacher the truth

quiz.en: You broke a plate and Mum asks who did it. You…
True or false? Sidq means truthfulness.
True or false? A sadiq always tells lies.
True or false? Muhammad ﷺ was the most truthful of all people.
True or false? It is important to admit and correct our mistakes.

think.q: Can you remember a time you told the truth even though it got you into trouble? How did you feel?
think.a: Brave and clean inside — and Allah was with you.

parents.summary: Sidq: always telling the truth, the same inside and out; lies spread like ink; the Prophet ﷺ was the most truthful.
parents.tip: When he tells a hard truth, thank him first — before dealing with the mistake.
